incidents.title: AuditTeam ransomware campaign deploys likely LLM-assisted OpsAgent tooling
incidents.targets: Organizations in at least seven countries
incidents.outcome: AuditTeam compromised organizations in at least seven countries. Its OpsAgent framework included a file-encryption module.
incidents.confidenceReason: Kaspersky identified code patterns in OpsAgent that suggest LLM-assisted development.
incidents.summary: Kaspersky tracked AuditTeam compromises from January through October 2026 and identified OpsAgent, a previously unknown modular framework. The evidence for AI use comes from the framework's code.
incidents.quote: Several code patterns suggest that a large language model, or LLM, a type of AI, helped write OpsAgent. All of its code-injection commands share a nearly identical structure and differ only in the number of arguments and the target process.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Kaspersky has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.

sources.title: Kaspersky uncovers AuditTeam ransomware campaign spanning Europe, Asia and Africa

incidents.title: Operation Bizarre Bazaar: hijacked LLM endpoints resold through a marketplace
incidents.actor: Actor using the aliases Hecker, Sakuya and LiveGamer101
incidents.targets: Exposed Ollama, vLLM and MCP endpoints
incidents.outcome: Access to exposed AI endpoints was resold across 30+ LLM providers.
incidents.confidenceReason: Pillar Security logged the sessions itself and its own report is cited.
incidents.summary: Pillar Security logged about 35,000 attack sessions scanning for exposed AI endpoints, validating access and reselling it through a marketplace.
incidents.quote: Pillar Security logged ~35,000 attack sessions scanning for exposed AI endpoints, validating access and reselling it via a marketplace covering 30+ LLM providers.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Pillar Security has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep, which AI Threat Watch restates.

incidents.title: AI-assisted phishing campaign harvesting victim data via browser permissions
incidents.outcome: Victim data harvested through browser permissions.
incidents.confidenceReason: Cyble: emojis in the script are 'increasingly ... observed in campaigns that use generative AI tools'. Thin artifact inference.
incidents.summary: Cyble reports a phishing framework that harvests victim data through browser permissions, with indicators that suggest AI-assisted development. The date is approximate.
incidents.quote: Indicators in the script also suggest AI-assisted development, reflecting how threat actors may be using generative AI tools to accelerate the creation of phishing frameworks.
incidents.singleSourceReason: Only Cyble has reported this operation among the sources found in the 2026-11-17 sweep.

incidents.title: Konni targets blockchain engineers with an AI-built PowerShell backdoor
incidents.outcome: Blockchain engineers were targeted with the backdoor.
incidents.confidenceReason: Check Point infers AI-assisted development from the malware's code; it reaches us through BleepingComputer.
incidents.summary: North Korea-linked Konni targeted blockchain engineers with a PowerShell backdoor that Check Point says strongly indicates AI-assisted development. BleepingComputer published on 24 January 2026.
incidents.quote: The researchers say that the PowerShell malware "strongly indicates AI-assisted development rather than traditional operator-authored malware."

incidents.title: UNC1069 hits crypto fintech with fake Zoom and apparent deepfake CEO video
incidents.targets: Cryptocurrency fintech and Web3 firms, macOS host
incidents.outcome: Seven malware families found on a macOS host.
incidents.confidenceReason: Mandiant says: 'Mandiant was unable to recover forensic evidence to independently verify the use of AI models in this specific instance'. The deepfake rests on the victim's report that the video 'appeared to be a deepfake'. Mandiant notes the actor's 'known use of AI tools by the threat actor for editing images or videos', but that is general, not about this incident.
incidents.summary: Telegram contact from a compromised executive account led to a spoofed Zoom with an apparent deepfake CEO and a ClickFix lure. Mandiant says the group also uses AI for lure material.
incidents.quote: a video of a CEO from another cryptocurrency company that appeared to be a deepfake

harness.note: AI used as assistant or tool, not as an agent harness
